title: Research project on maths ability

paragraphs.text: Now turn to section three on page five.
Part three.
You will hear a student called Aya discussing her research project about maths ability with her tutor.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-three.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-three.

Right, Aya. Last time we met, you decided to choose skills and attitudes in learning maths as the focus of your research project, and you were thinking of splitting it into two sections. Is that right?
Uh, yes. I decided to start by looking at people's attitude to maths and then go on to research how people actually solve different math problems.
Great. Now, what research methods did you use?

Well, I explored lots of different techniques and actually tried out things like sending out questionnaires, but then I opted for a different approach. I thought face-to-face interviews would be more appropriate because you can look at things in more depth when you're actually with the person.
Hmm. How many participants did you have?
Quite a few, which meant interviewing was pretty demanding work. Twenty-five altogether. Uh, fourteen men and eleven women.
How did you identify them?

Well, they were all students at this college, and what I did was send round a really short questionnaire by email asking whether people like maths, and these twenty-five answered, "Not at all," which is what I needed.
So you followed them up?

Yeah, and arranged to interview them. Now, the first question I asked them was, "How good do you think you are at maths?" And I got these results. A pretty even split at either end of the continuum. Uh, twenty percent for both good and poor, and the majority in the middle. And I should emphasize that for this, there were no distinct differences between men and women.
Did those figures surprise you?
Hmm, I wouldn't say so. What did shock me was how violently anti-maths as a subject they were. It wasn't what I'd expected at all.
Yes, I can imagine.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-four to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-four to thirty.
Anyway, the next part of my interview asked about their experiences of learning maths and why they had become so negative about it.
Mm-hmm.

Yeah. Interesting, isn't it?

00:04:33,560

Mm-hmm.

00:04:44,060

Yes. That's been my experience as well.

00:04:46,340

Mm-hmm. And for the men, they found problems because they had this strong belief that you have to be born with a talent for the subject to be any good at maths.

00:04:56,500

00:04:58,880

00:05:21,580

Of what?

Good mathematicians?

How interesting. I've noticed that actually how I work best.

00:06:19,920

Yeah.

And what about the weaker ones?

00:06:23,420

Well, I have to say the strategy they used was to give up immediately after reading the question, I'm afraid.

Well, that's extremely interesting, Aya. Now, had you thought about actually...
